Fig. 10. Relative error of the surface area estimate calculated for balls of increasing radii when using A1Z0.2118 as suggested in Ref. [1]. (b) shows the same information as (a) in a log–log scale. We use the same approach as in Section 5.1, in order to ﬁnd an optimal distribution of surface area between cases c1, c5, and c9. Since planar surfaces do not provide enough information to give a unique solution, we need some type of non-planar objects to perform the optimization on. We feel that the most natural objects to use for this purpose are digitized balls of ﬁnite radii. Balls are the simplest of ﬁnite- sized objects, they are rotationally symmetric, and their surfaces have a constant curvature.
